title: IDEAL-Age: an interpretable deep learning framework for single-cell resolution profiling of immunological aging.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: CELLxGENE (a public single-cell data portal) API metadata: AIDA (Asian Immune Diversity Atlas) Data Freeze v2 has 1,265,624 cells, 625 donors, one 14.24 GB H5AD (single-cell file format) file. OneK1K has 1,248,980 cells, 981 donors, one 4.43 GB H5AD file, with age stored as 'N-year-old stage'. Zenodo record 20744504 holds only code (118 KB zip). I did not download any H5AD file because both exceed the 50 MB cap.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Training split: 500 AIDA and 784 OneK1K donors (an 80% split, consistent with the 625 and 981 donors on CELLxGENE). External cohorts: HCA (Human Cell Atlas), Sound Life, CIMA. Benchmark of 35 methods. Reported errors: internal test PCC (Pearson correlation) 0.878 with MAE (mean absolute error) 6.91 years; external test PCC 0.819 with MAE 7.81 years. Supplementary tables S1–S8 were not retrievable (Europe PMC timed out).

a1_downloadable.note: CELLxGENE H5AD files are public with no login (checked the API asset listing). CIMA is on CNGBdb and siAge on Synapse; their access terms were not checked.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Chronological age is a donor metadata field (development_stage, e.g. '19-year-old stage'; seen in the OneK1K API metadata). It needs a simple string-to-number parse.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are per-cell expression counts inside the H5AD files (from the paper and the CELLxGENE schema; matrices not opened).

a4_units_stated.note: Age is in years. Counts follow the CELLxGENE schema (raw counts in .raw).

a5_enough_rows.note: The real unit is the donor: 625 AIDA + 981 OneK1K = 1,606 labelled donors (API metadata), plus external cohorts. That is just above the 1,500 regression threshold; millions of cells do not count as independent rows.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 18.7 GB raw H5AD; under 100 MB after per-donor pseudobulk (expression summed per donor and cell type)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw files exceed the laptop budget, but backed-mode streaming to per-donor-by-cell-type pseudobulk is a simple reduction route.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The paper's 500 and 784 training donors equal 80% of the 625 and 981 donors listed by the CELLxGENE API.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is self-reported chronological age from cohort metadata. It is not a model output and is not derived from expression.

B1.why: Several cohort H5AD files with different annotations; donor ID join within each file (API metadata).

B2.why: H5AD loads via anndata, but 14 GB needs backed mode; age needs a string parse.

B3.why: Age is comparable everywhere, but expression has cross-cohort batch effects (the paper itself says so).

B4.why: Age recorded as integer years; no censoring seen in OneK1K stage labels.

B5.why: AIDA v1 and v2 overlap; you must pick one freeze. Otherwise one sample per donor (paper).

B6.why: CELLxGENE schema standardizes and documents the metadata columns.

C1.why: Ancestry-transfer question informative either way, but mostly a race to beat 11 existing clocks.

C2.why: IDEAL-Age, sc-ImmuAging, scAgeClock all open, evaluated on external cohorts; 35-method benchmark exists.

C3.why: Only weak diversity angle (Asian vs European transfer); IDEAL-Age already trains on both.

C4.why: Chronological age is free to know; value is only as a proxy for biological age.

C5.why: Published numbers: internal MAE 6.91 and external MAE 7.81 years (paper).

D1.why: Geneformer and scGPT, open single-cell foundation models, fit PBMC (blood immune cell) data.

D2.why: Embedding ~2.5M cells on CPU is days; would need subsampling cells per donor.

D3.why: IDEAL-Age MIT; Geneformer Apache-2.0; CELLxGENE data CC-BY.

E1.why: Leave-one-cohort-out split (AIDA, OneK1K, HCA, Sound Life, CIMA) prevents donor and batch leakage.

E2.why: Five-plus cohorts, plus AIDA's six ancestry groups (API title).

E3.why: Predicting each donor's age as the training-set mean gives a dummy MAE.

E4.why: No repeat samples from the same donor in the training cohorts, so the noise floor can't be estimated directly.

E5.why: Known effect: naive CD8 T-cell fraction falls with age; the model must recover it.

E6.why: Shuffle ages across donors; ablate cell-type composition versus expression.

E7.why: HCA, Sound Life and CIMA external cohorts exist (paper).

E8.why: IDEAL-Age code on GitHub/Zenodo; reproduce its internal test MAE of 6.91 years.

G1.why: Ensembl gene IDs in CELLxGENE files; donor IDs link to OneK1K genotypes.

G2.why: OneK1K eQTL (gene-expression genetic variant) genotypes are plausible partners; their access was not checked.

G3.why: One donor per age label; clean one-to-one join.

G4.why: Genetics of immune-age acceleration is interesting but noisy at about 1,000 donors.

H1.why: Continuous age 19–96 covers the full range; no selection on outcome.

H2.why: Two main cohorts (Australian European, Asian); few donors under 19 or over 77.

H4.why: Authors state the age-extreme scarcity and batch effects explicitly.

I1.why: Aging and immunology community broadly; no specific group whose decision changes.

I2.why: Another clock marginally changes anything given 11 exist.

I3.why: MAE on chronological age is only a proxy for biological aging.

I4.why: PLSR on cell composition already gives a decent clock; ML adds some.

J1.why: Real set-based modelling, grouped cross-cohort splits, foundation-model embeddings.

J2.why: Age is intuitive, but judging cell-type attributions needs immunology input.

J3.why: A cross-cohort re-benchmark is shareable, but likely confirms published results.

existing_models.name: IDEAL-Age (this paper; DeepSets attention plus AutoGluon ensemble)
existing_models.score_and_split: Internal test (random 20% of donors): PCC 0.878, MAE 6.91 years; external cohorts (HCA, Sound Life, CIMA): PCC 0.819, MAE 7.81 years.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Too few independent cohorts at age extremes (<19, >77); cross-cohort batch effects; rare cell types underrepresented.

existing_models.name: sc-ImmuAging (Nature Aging 2025, cell-type-specific PBMC clocks)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 1,081 donors aged 18–97; benchmarked in IDEAL-Age (exact numbers not retrieved).

existing_models.name: scAgeClock (npj Aging 2026, gated multi-head attention)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 16M cells across 40+ tissues; about half of tissue cell types have MAE under 10 years.

backbone.name: Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome foundation model)
backbone.hardware: CPU feasible only with subsampled cells per donor (e.g. 500 cells × 1,600 donors); full set needs a GPU.

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do inherited genetic variants explain why some people's immune cells look older than their chronological age?

controls.positive_control: Recover the known age-related loss of naive CD8 T cells and the rise in effector memory cells.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle donor ages; performance must collapse to the mean-age MAE.
controls.external_validation: Leave-one-cohort-out across AIDA, OneK1K, HCA, Sound Life, CIMA.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts the chronological age of adults aged about 19–77 from blood immune-cell transcriptomes in 10x-profiled Asian and European cohorts, with accuracy dropping across labs and at age extremes.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression from a person's blood immune cells to predict their age, and test transfer across ancestries.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-donor sets of blood immune-cell transcriptomes; 1,606 donors in the two main cohorts (verified via API metadata).
plain_idea.predict: Donor chronological age in years, from cohort records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gaps between predicted and true age could flag accelerated immune aging (e.g. in lupus). But open clocks already do this, so a new one changes little.

more_or_better_data.why: We would use the same AIDA plus OneK1K data (1,606 donors) that IDEAL-Age used; sc-ImmuAging used 1,081 donors and scAgeClock 16M cells.

confidence_score.why: No repeat samples from the same donor in the training cohorts to calibrate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: IDEAL-Age (2026) and scAgeClock (2026) are recent attention models, open, and evaluated on external cohorts.

guaranteed_improvement.why: IDEAL-Age already uses AIDA and OneK1K and validates on HCA, Sound Life and CIMA; there is no unused, same-protocol data to add.

label_elsewhere.sources: Donor age is in CELLxGENE metadata for many PBMC datasets (seen in API metadata for AIDA and OneK1K); Sound Life and CIMA cohorts per the paper.
label_elsewhere.why: Age is recorded for nearly every human single-cell dataset, so external test cohorts are plentiful.

ml_idea: Leave-one-cohort-out immune age regression from per-donor single-cell PBMC (blood immune cell) data, with Geneformer embeddings pooled per donor, compared against IDEAL-Age.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: backed-mode H5AD streaming to pseudobulk; Geneformer on CPU with about 800k subsampled cells at roughly 10 cells/s.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Run released IDEAL-Age on AIDA held out by ancestry group; if MAE already matches within-cohort MAE, no transfer gap is left to study.

verdict_reason: Data is clean and open (1,606 donors), but the single-cell immune-clock field is saturated: IDEAL-Age, sc-ImmuAging and scAgeClock are open, recent and tested on external cohorts. We'd re-use the same cohorts with no data edge.
